> Curated papers, systems, and datasets for Text-to-SQL that can recognize ambiguity, ask useful questions, and decline unsupported requests.

Natural-language questions do not always determine one SQL query, and a database cannot answer every request. This collection focuses on how NL2SQL agents detect these situations, resolve them through interaction or additional evidence, and evaluate when to answer or abstain.

[**Explore the interactive catalog →**](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/) · [Browse papers](papers/README.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmark-matrix.md) · [Try the examples](examples/README.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Updated **2026-10-31**. Each paper includes a concise summary, publication status, public sources, and a verification date. Core work and adjacent methods are marked separately. Resource counts include clearly labeled benchmark designs whose artifacts are not yet verified released.

## Scope

We include work that directly studies ambiguity, underspecification, answerability, clarification, or abstention in natural-language querying of relational databases. We also include selected verification, uncertainty, and contextual-grounding methods when their relevance to those problems is explicit. Generic SQL-generation systems and broad agent frameworks belong in the related collections unless they provide a concrete capability relevant to this scope.

An ambiguous request, an unsupported request, a model error, and a valid query returning no rows are different cases. Likewise, a publication, an announced repository, released artifacts, and independently reproduced results are different kinds of evidence. The annotations preserve these distinctions; inclusion is not a deployment endorsement.

## Recent additions

| Year | Paper / venue | Concise summary | Code / data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2025 | [Leveraging LLM-Generated Schema Descriptions for Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Data](papers/README.md#sqd-schema-descriptions)<br>COLING 2025<br><em>core</em> | SQD trains an encoder to predict question-schema relevance using LLM-generated schema descriptions, then thresholds those scores to detect unanswerable requests before SQL generation. Evaluation uses EHRSQL 2024. The paper identifies failures requiring database-content checks and leaves generalization to new schemas untested; schema relevance does not establish downstream SQL correctness. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#sqd-schema-descriptions) |
| 2025 | [RAG-based Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Text-to-SQL](papers/README.md#raqad)<br>CIKM 2025<br><em>core</em> | RaQAD retrieves semantically similar examples for few-shot LLM prompts that classify whether clinical database questions are answerable, without additional model training. The institutional abstract reports clinical experiments and adaptation to schema changes. This supports inclusion as an answerability-screening method; detailed evaluation conditions, downstream SQL correctness and clarification behavior were not verified from full text. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#raqad) |
| 2026 | [AtomSQL: Interactive Disambiguation of NL-to-SQL via User-Guided Atom-Level Alignment](papers/README.md#atomsql)<br>PVLDB 19(12), 2026 demonstration<br><em>core</em> | Exposes disagreements between SQL candidates as clause-level atoms aligned with phrases in the question, then uses user selections to adjust future preferences. The demonstration makes alternative interpretations inspectable, but resolution is limited to candidates supplied by the active models: users must reformulate when none expresses their intent. | [Code](https://github.com/aritra741/AtomSQL)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#atomsql) |
| 2026 | [Same SQL, Different Decision: Aggregate Risk Hides Cross-Lingual Instability in Text-to-SQL Verification](papers/README.md#same-sql-different-decision)<br>ORACLE workshop at EMNLP 2026<br><em>core</em> | Holds candidate SQL, schema and execution labels fixed while varying question language to audit execute-or-defer decisions. Similar aggregate risk can hide different queries being executed; the study tests score adjustment and translation to English. Results concern English-generated SQL and two main verifiers, with execution-match labels and imperfect translation limiting semantic and end-to-end claims. | [Code](https://github.com/tokenledger/same-sql-different-decision) · [Data](https://github.com/tokenledger/same-sql-different-decision/tree/main/data/big)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#same-sql-different-decision) |
| 2025 | [Grounding LLMs for Database Exploration: Intent Scoping and Paraphrasing for Robust NL2SQL](papers/README.md#intent-scoping-paraphrasing)<br>AIDB 2025 (VLDB workshop)<br><em>core</em> | Classifies database requests as fully answerable, partially answerable or out of scope, and uses entity-preserving paraphrases to improve NL2SQL robustness. The scoping and paraphrasing components depend on upstream entity recognition; the paper leaves integration with complex joins and nested queries to future work, so the results do not establish complete conversational recovery. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#intent-scoping-paraphrasing) |
| 2026 | [Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs](papers/README.md#schema-free-query-logs)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>adjacent</em> | Builds a graph of schema relationships and business entities from query logs, then retrieves context for SQL generation in poorly documented databases. Its BEAVER experiment instead builds edges from schema metadata, so it does not independently test log-based discovery. Executability and judge preferences do not establish complete intent resolution or abstention ability. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#schema-free-query-logs) |
| 2026 | [An OMOP-Based Open-Source Text-to-SQL Benchmark Dataset](papers/README.md#text-to-omop)<br>ClinicalNLP at LREC 2026<br><em>core</em> | Evaluates SQL generation or explicit abstention over synthetic OMOP data using concept-normalized questions and EHRSQL-derived templates and unanswerables. Execution and penalty-based reliability scores test the specified SQL-or-refuse contract; raw-text entity linking, ambiguous concept resolution and clinical deployment safety remain outside the demonstrated evaluation. | [Code](https://github.com/red1dwarf/TEXT-TO-OMOP) · [Data](https://github.com/red1dwarf/TEXT-TO-OMOP/tree/main/DATA)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#text-to-omop) |
| 2026 | [Building SQL Equivalence Proofs from Query Rewrite Rules](papers/README.md#equitrace)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>adjacent</em> | EquiTrace constructs replayable SQL-equivalence derivations by aligning query plans and composing admitted rewrite rules under schema constraints. Proof validity depends on those rules and applicability conditions; unsuccessful bounded search returns UNKNOWN, not inequivalence. This supports semantic evaluation of candidate/reference SQL pairs without establishing that the reference captures the user’s intent. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#equitrace) |

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for material changes and the [dated search records](docs/search-log/README.md) for coverage and unresolved leads. This is a living curated collection, not a claim of complete literature coverage.

## Contributing

Suggest a resource or correction through an [issue](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/issues/new/choose) or pull request. Include a primary source and explain the connection to ambiguity or unanswerability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and checks.

The canonical records are [papers.json](data/papers.json) and [resources.json](data/resources.json). The indexes are generated, so contributors only need to maintain one record per work.
